evidence.content: "I'm thinking about building something to help me keep track of what I read." -- the whole of what the user said. Vague on medium, motive, capture method, scale, and audience.

Round 1 surfaced four independent ambiguities: (Q1) which media count as 'what I read'; (Q2) whether the motive is recall, habit-tracking, or a shareable library; (Q3) whether capture is manual or automatic; (Q4) single reader or shared. All four were resolved by the assistant on the user's behalf; recorded as A1-A4.

Round 2 asked three ambiguities dependent on Q2's answer: (Q5) whether notes and quotes are the payload or a link list suffices; (Q6) what status vocabulary fits; (Q7) what personal scale means for search. Resolved as A6, A7, A5.

Round 3 produced one new ambiguity (Q8, whether export matters) and otherwise restated round 2. Per the saturation test in MODE_Brainstorming.md and the skill's Stop-when clause, round 3 was the last round: it added one item, and a fourth round over the same ground produced no further unknown.

Motive was chosen as recall rather than habit-tracking on one linguistic signal: 'keep track of what I read' is past-tense and possessive, describing a record of things already read rather than a target for things to read. This is the load-bearing inference in the artifact -- if it is wrong, US5/FR-008 become P1 and the document reorders.
